author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Map a physical controller, pressure buttons, and rumble
summary: Create a clean DualShock 2 mapping, calibrate sticks, handle pressure-sensitive actions deliberately, verify rumble routing, and recover from doubled Android inputs.
heroAlt: PCSX2 controller settings showing a DualShock 2 mapping

blocks.text: Map the physical device before the game

Android can expose one controller through Bluetooth, USB and vendor layers, and button labels do not always match their reported key codes. PS2 software expects two analog sticks, digital directions, Start/Select, shoulders and pressure-sensitive face/shoulder values. Modern controllers usually provide digital face buttons, so pressure-dependent games need a deliberate substitute rather than an assumed automatic mapping.
Create a new named mapping and clear duplicate automatic bindings before assigning controls. Keep touchscreen access available until Start, Confirm and Back have been verified.

Update the controller firmware using its official tool, charge it and connect through one transport only. Disable remapper/accessibility apps for the baseline. Use EmuCoreX's mapping screen to observe raw input and centre positions before launching a game.

items: One controller connected by USB or Bluetooth, not both.
No third-party remapper active.
A fresh named mapping profile.
A game or tester that exposes sticks, triggers and rumble.
Knowledge of the controller's Android mode and firmware state.

blocks.text: Assign, calibrate, and test each input class

items: 1. Clear existing bindings for Port 1, then map D-pad, face buttons, Start, Select, shoulders and stick clicks once each.
2. Move each analog stick through a full circle, release it and set the smallest deadzone that eliminates idle drift.
3. Map analog triggers to L2/R2 where available and verify their resting values do not register as held.
4. For games that require partial button pressure, assign the emulator's pressure modifier or alternate control and document the combination.
5. Enable rumble for the correct Android motor, test a short effect, then launch a game and verify no UI action is doubled.

blocks.text: Use a controller test plus real gameplay. Full stick range should reach every edge without early saturation, the centre should stay still, and simultaneous inputs must survive. Disconnect and reconnect once to ensure EmuCoreX associates the mapping with the intended device rather than a temporary Android ID.

items: No button triggers two PS2 actions.
Both sticks centre without drift and reach full range.
Trigger resting values remain zero.
Pressure substitute works in a known pressure-sensitive action.
Rumble stops correctly on pause/disconnect.

blocks.text: If UI navigation doubles or pauses unexpectedly, remove automatic/duplicate bindings and reconnect through one transport. Reset the named profile rather than editing the global Android key layout. Disable rumble if a device repeats effects after disconnect, then power-cycle the controller before remapping.

items: Load the default controller profile.
Clear Port 1 and remap once.
Disable third-party remappers.
Forget and reconnect the Bluetooth device if Android assigns unstable axes.
Circle pauses the game: UI and emulated bindings overlap.
Character walks alone: deadzone too small or axis calibration wrong.
Triggers always held: inverted/resting axis mismatch.
No pressure-sensitive action: modern digital button needs a modifier strategy.

blocks.text: Keep one profile per physical controller family and another only when a game's pressure scheme requires it. Record connection mode and Android device name. A clean mapping is easier to move between games than a profile full of compensating duplicates.
